questions.question: What is the formula for the number of diagonals in a convex polygon with n sides?
options: n^2 - n
questions.rationale: Subtracting the n sides themselves from all C(n,2) point-pairs gives n(n-3)/2 diagonals.

Why does diagonal counting matter in figure-counting problems?
options: Diagonals never affect the figure count
Diagonals can create additional intersection points and sub-figures inside a polygon that must also be accounted for
Diagonals only matter for circles
Diagonals always double the total figure count
questions.rationale: Diagonals drawn inside a polygon create new intersection points and divide the polygon into additional sub-figures, all of which need to be included in a full count.

questions.question: What complicates counting figures in 'star and overlapping figures' problems?
options: Stars never contain any valid figures
The overlapping lines create many additional intersection points and smaller sub-regions that must each be carefully identified
Overlapping figures always cancel each other out
Star figures are always symmetric and require no counting
questions.rationale: The many overlapping lines in a star figure create numerous extra intersection points and smaller regions, each of which must be carefully identified as part of a full count.

questions.question: When two circles overlap, how many regions do they divide the plane into (inside the circles' outlines, generic case)?
questions.rationale: Two overlapping circles create 3 regions: the two non-overlapping crescent areas, plus the shared overlapping region in the middle.

questions.question: What is the key difference between 'circle counting' and 'counting regions' in an overlapping-circles figure?
options: They are exactly the same thing
Circle counting counts how many circle shapes are present, while region counting counts how many distinct enclosed areas the circles' boundaries divide the plane into
Region counting only applies to squares
Circle counting always gives a larger number than region counting
questions.rationale: Circle counting tallies the circle shapes themselves, while region counting tallies the distinct enclosed areas their boundaries create — these are different questions with different answers.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'counting regions' and 'counting figures'?
options: There is no difference between the two
A region is any enclosed area, while a 'figure' typically refers to a specific recognizable shape (like a triangle or square) among those regions
Figures are always larger than regions
Regions can never be figures
questions.rationale: A region is simply any enclosed area created by the diagram's lines, while a 'figure' usually refers to a specific recognizable shape — not every region is necessarily a named figure.

questions.question: How many unit squares (1x1) exist in a 3x3 grid?
questions.rationale: A 3-row by 3-column grid of unit cells contains 3 x 3 = 9 unit squares.
